title: Mid-Season Showdown! Tournament cEDH Gameplay: Ral v Bluefarm v Bluefarm v Magda

event.name: Mid-Season Showdown, Topdeck Championship Series 2026
event.field_note: Invitational-adjacent event: top ~60 players from the 2026 Championship Series; commentators (Eric, Max P) stress everyone at the table is a top-cut-caliber pilot

players.note: Seat labels confirmed from stream overlay via frame sampling 2026-08-24: Joseph-Ral top-left (Player 1), Tyler-Blue Farm top-right (Player 2), Ashton-Blue Farm bottom-right (Player 3), Natalie-Magda bottom-left (Player 4). Overlay uses first names only.

extraction.method: manual LLM read of timestamped auto-captions (data/transcripts/sZA0KqXCGrY.txt) covering commentary, player audio during the storm turn, and a post-game winner interview; card names repaired against the four published decklists; targeted video frame sampling (yt-dlp --download-sections + ffmpeg stills at 14:50, 17:55, 22:35, 24:30) for the stream overlay, seat order, life totals, and board checks; Ral, Monsoon Mage // Ral, Leyline Prodigy oracle text verified via one Scryfall lookup to decode the loyalty math
extraction.gameplay_window: 14:44-29:06 of the VOD; live play runs ~14:53 to ~24:35 ('that's GG's'); 24:35-29:06 is on-air post-mortem; 33:00-42:00 is a winner interview with Joseph that confirms his mulligan and line and is used as a primary source
caveats: Auto-captions only; player audio exists for the winning storm turn, which makes that turn unusually well documented for this corpus, but crosstalk still garbles several card names.
Life totals read from a phone counter that faces the players, so the top row is upside down on stream; digits flipped mentally (a displayed '6' for Player 1 is a real 9).
Speaker attribution during the storm turn is inferred; Joseph is the only sustained speaker.
The game is one turn cycle plus one turn, so most of the pod's decision content is in mulligans and the single response window, not in board development.

games.seat_order_confidence: high; confirmed by stream overlay quadrant labels and Player 1-4 life counter frame at 14:50 and 22:35
games.win_turn_basis: winner's own turns elapsed; commentators and Joseph both state the other three players never got a turn 2, so the table played 5 player-turns total (relevant when comparing against Forge, which counts player-turns)
games.win_method: Turn-2 storm kill from seat 1: Treasonous Ogre mana plus Windfall refuel, Mental Misstep protecting the Windfall from Swan Song, Grapeshot at storm 11 clearing blockers-to-interaction, Ral flipping to Ral, Leyline Prodigy entering with 8 loyalty and ultimating (-8, exile top 8 castable free) directly into Underworld Breach + Pyretic Ritual + Quiet Speculation (binning Past in Flames); table concedes with the Underworld Breach + Brain Freeze loop demonstrated ('Breach and freeze' per commentary)
games.win_confirmed_by: commentator call at 24:35, on-air post-mortem, and Joseph's own winner interview at 33:00+

mulligans.detail: mulligan to 4, kept: unnamed rainbow land, Mana Vault, Treasonous Ogre, Windfall (self-reported in interview). En route he saw and correctly shipped a six of Mountain, Gemstone Caverns, Springleaf Drum + three dig spells as 'really slow in that pod' with bad colors.

mulliganed at least once; Joseph reports one shipped hand was 'two lands... two pieces of interaction and do nothing', not keepable in Blue Farm going second; final hand small ('his hand's just too low'), contained Swan Song and a drawn Gemstone Caverns. Exact final hand size not stated.

kept (count unstated, likely 7): Gemstone Caverns (played on turn 0), Vampiric Tutor, Swan Song, additional interaction. Commentators call it a good keep; the debate is entirely about how he sequenced it.

kept 'a relatively quick hand' (judge-fed info): fast development, dwarves/dorks, 'small amount of interaction'. Both commentators and Joseph flag this keep as the pod's second critical error: against seat-1 Ral the Magda mulligan 'really needed to be for something to slow the game down' (Damping Sphere, Magus of the Moon, a lightning bolt for Ral).

key_line.play: rainbow land, Mana Vault, Treasonous Ogre; Ogre mana into a dig spell (Witch's Mark per commentary, draw-then-discard), discarding a dead card; digs find a fetch land for blue plus Mental Misstep
key_line.repair: 'frenetic searcher' (the discarded card) unidentified; Witch's Mark is in the list and matches the commentator's read
key_line.note: line reconstructed from Joseph's interview at 33:43-34:20; commentators at 14:55: 'the Mana Vaults have played to set up the wheel on the next turn'

key_line.note: self-inflicted; confirmed twice (commentary 17:42 'he has no color' and Joseph's interview 37:19)

key_line.play: land development only; holds Vampiric Tutor and Swan Song
develops dorks: at least one Automaton artifact creature on board by end of turn (silver-frame artifact creature visible in the 17:55 frame; name unreadable)
key_line.repair: later Grapeshot target 'the Sanctum Automaton' -> Universal Automaton or Adaptive Automaton (both in list); two Grapeshot instances were aimed at it, which fits 2-toughness Adaptive Automaton slightly better

key_line.play: responds to Windfall: cracks a fetch, Vampiric Tutor (tutored card per Joseph's interview: 'mystic study'), and casts Swan Song targeting Windfall
key_line.repair: 'mystic study' -> Rhystic Study (phonetic match; Mystic Remora also in list and also discussed, so identity is genuinely ambiguous between the two draw engines)

key_line.play: Mental Misstep counters the Swan Song ('Here's what I'm going to step on the Swan Song'); Windfall resolves; storm turn begins

key_line.play: storm sequence with player audio: Gitaxian Probe targeting an opponent (Ral flip trigger + a second trigger he calls 'storm trigger', likely Storm-Kiln Artist treasure), loses at least one Ral flip ('I lose life'); life frames show Joseph at 9 by 22:35 and 6 by 24:30 (Ogre + Probe + lost flips)
key_line.repair: 'storm trigger' on a Probe is not a real storm trigger; Storm-Kiln Artist (in list) is the best candidate source

key_line.play: Grapeshot as the 11th storm spell (he has cast nine, opponents two): 10 copies; original plus one copy kill Natalie's Automaton, nine copies at Ashton's face
key_line.repair: 'Sanctum Automaton' -> Universal/Adaptive Automaton; face target inferred as Ashton from the life frame (40 -1 fetch -2 vamp -9 = 28, matching the counter exactly) and his quip 'I don't play Necro[potence]' (true only of Ashton's list)

key_line.play: wins a flip, Ral transforms: Ral, Leyline Prodigy enters with 2 base + 6 (instants/sorceries cast this turn) = exactly 8 loyalty; immediately ultimates: -8 exiles his top eight (Pyretic Ritual, Abandon Attachments, Gamble, Quiet Speculation, land(s), and evidently Underworld Breach) castable free this turn; Ral hits 0 loyalty, dies, and Joseph deliberately puts him in the graveyard rather than the command zone
key_line.repair: 'Abandon Hope' -> Abandon Attachments; 'Quirion Speculation' -> Quiet Speculation; loyalty math verified against the printed card
key_line.note: commentator: 'almost like Joe was clairvoyant... I'll put all of them in the graveyard because I'm just going to go get the Breach now'

key_line.play: Underworld Breach (storm 12, cast free off the ultimate), Pyretic Ritual free (storm 13, add RRR), Quiet Speculation targeting himself putting up to three flashback spells in his graveyard including Past in Flames
key_line.repair: 'notably passive flames' -> Past in Flames; published list holds only two flashback cards (Past in Flames, Lava Dart), so 'three flashback spells' implies either two targets or list drift
key_line.confidence: high for the cards named, medium for completeness

key_line.play: next cast begins ('Abandon Attachments triggers?') and the table concedes: 'Well, kids, that's GG's' (24:33); commentary names the demonstrated kill 'Breach and freeze' = Underworld Breach + Brain Freeze
key_line.note: win by concession with the deterministic loop shown, not played to completion on camera

magda_observations.note: Zero Magda activations and zero fetches: Natalie took exactly one turn (dork development) before the game ended, and Magda herself was likely never cast. Her only board presence, an Automaton dork, died to Grapeshot copies. For the pilot-study comparison this game contributes a seat-4 Magda data point where the archetype's engine never turned on; the actionable content is her keep (fast hand, no interaction) being labeled an error against seat-1 turbo.

headline_features.mull_to_four_wins: the winner mulliganed to 4 and won on his second turn; commentators note the deck is 'built to mulligan that low'
interaction_events_spoken: Mental Misstep counters Swan Song on the Windfall
Vampiric Tutor response window used for a draw engine instead of interaction
Grapeshot copies kill a Magda dork and burn seat 3 for 9
headline_features.study_relevance: This is a human-ceiling floor case for speed: seat-1 turbo storm ends the game at winner-turn 2 / table-turn 5. It also documents the human skill layer the sim AI lacks: pod-aware mulligans (the two players who kept greedy/engine hands are named as the reason the win went through), holding interaction for the named threat, and sequencing a tutor before vs during the threat turn.

What exactly did Ashton Vampiric Tutor for: 'mystic study' reads as Rhystic Study phonetically, but Mystic Remora is the card everyone says he wanted; both are in his list.
Was Magda, Brazen Outlaw cast on Natalie's single turn? No spoken or legible-frame evidence either way; treated as not cast.
Was the 'storm trigger' Joseph announced on Gitaxian Probe a Storm-Kiln Artist treasure trigger? Best fit, unverified.
Tyler's exact mulligan count and final hand size.
Identity of the card Joseph discarded to the turn-1 dig spell (captions: 'bad frenetic searcher').
Quiet Speculation's full target set: 'up to three flashback spells' vs only two flashback cards in the published list (Past in Flames, Lava Dart); possible list drift.
